records.headline: FAA AD 2026-10-06 supersedes 2020-24-08: Trent 700 HPT blade corrosion-fatigue replacement, effective June 12, 2026
records.summary: The FAA superseded AD 2020-24-08 with new AD 2026-10-06 for Rolls-Royce Deutschland RB211 Trent 768-60, 772-60, and 772B-60 engines (Trent 700 series, A330 powerplant), effective June 12, 2026. The AD responds to high levels of corrosion fatigue in HPT blades that could result in blade cracking and release, with risk of aborted takeoff and in-flight shutdown events; it requires removal of certain engines from service and HPT blade replacement before specified flight-cycle thresholds, with an optional engine modification as terminating action.

references.ref_number: AD 2026-10-06 (Amendment 39-23346; Docket No. FAA-2026-4635; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-00213-E)
references.effectivity: Rolls-Royce Deutschland RB211 Trent 768-60, 772-60, and 772B-60 engines as identified in EASA AD 2018-0291R1, dated February 24, 2025 (Trent 772C-60 excluded — no FAA type certificate)
references.fetched_text_snippet: affected blades on RRD Model RB211 Trent 700 engines have been subject to high levels of corrosion fatigue, which could result in blade cracking and eventual release with consequent aborted take-off and in-flight shut-down events.

records.oem_regulator_position: FAA: unsafe condition addressed by replacement of HPT blades before exceeding specified flight cycles since new, with an optional engine modification eliminating the need for repetitive replacement; this AD incorporates EASA AD 2018-0291R1 by reference.
records.root_cause: High-pressure turbine blades on certain Trent 700 (RB211 Trent 768-60/772-60/772B-60) engines subject to high levels of corrosion fatigue, dependent on environmental, operational, and individual blade conditions; risk of blade cracking and release with consequent damage and reduced control of the airplane.

records.headline: FAA AD 2026-12-05: A350 primary flight control actuators exposed to overload during acceptance testing; effective July 20, 2026
records.summary: The FAA published final AD 2026-12-05 (Federal Register doc 2026-11975) for all Airbus A350-941 and -1041 airplanes, confirming that certain primary flight control actuators (servo controls, electrical backup hydraulic actuators, electro-hydrostatic actuators) were exposed to mechanical overloads during the manufacturing acceptance test procedure, reducing fatigue life. The AD requires replacement of affected actuators and prohibits installation of affected parts; published in the Federal Register June 15, 2026 (within window), with a July 20, 2026 effective date.

references.effectivity: All Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and -1041 airplanes, certificated in any category
references.fetched_text_snippet: certain primary flight control actuators (servo controls, electrical backup hydraulic actuators, and electro-hydrostatic actuators) have been exposed to mechanical overloads during the acceptance test procedure, leading to reduced fatigue life

records.oem_regulator_position: FAA/EASA: replacement of affected parts with serviceable parts required; installation of affected parts prohibited. EASA AD 2025-0152 (dated July 18, 2025) is the underlying MCAI, incorporated by reference. FAA estimates 38 U.S.-registered airplanes affected, at $850 per airplane.
records.root_cause: During production, certain primary flight control actuators were exposed to mechanical overloads during the acceptance test procedure, leading to reduced fatigue life; uncorrected, this could result in actuator failure, loss of control of control surfaces, or hydraulic system loss.

records.headline: FAA AD 2026-09-14: A350 oxygen generator retaining clamp obsolescence/incorrect torque spec; effective June 18, 2026
records.summary: FAA AD 2026-09-14 (FR doc 2026-09659), effective June 18, 2026, applies to all Airbus A350-941 and -1041 airplanes. It addresses obsolescence of the clamp holding the chemical oxygen generator in its container: Collins introduced a replacement clamp from another manufacturer with a different locking-torque specification that was not properly reflected in Airbus documentation, risking damage to the oxygen generator housing if installed at the wrong torque. The AD requires replacing the affected clamp, prohibits use of an outdated maintenance task revision, and prohibits installation of affected parts.

records.headline: FAA AD 2026-10-19: A330 standby fuel pump dormant failure can trap unusable fuel; effective June 8, 2026 (outside window)
records.summary: FAA AD 2026-10-19 (FR doc 2026-10272), effective June 8, 2026, applies to all Airbus A330-200/-200F/-300/-841/-941 series airplanes. It addresses a dormant (undetected) failure mode in which a standby fuel pump could trap a quantity of fuel in the aft section of an inner tank, risking overestimation of usable fuel onboard and subsequent uncommanded in-flight dual engine shutdown. The AD requires repetitive operational checks of standby fuel pumps and corrective action, and limits installation of affected parts.

records.headline: Proposed FAA AD: A330 P2F freighter-conversion flightcrew oxygen system insufficient for ETOPS-180 with four crew (comment period closed June 15, 2026)
records.summary: A proposed FAA AD (NPRM, Docket FAA-2026-3873) applies only to Airbus A330-200/-300 series airplanes converted from passenger to freighter configuration under FAA STC ST04038NY (Elbe Flugzeugwerke P2F conversion). The FAA found that on these specifically modified airplanes, a flightcrew oxygen system supplied by a single oxygen cylinder is insufficient for ETOPS-180 operation with four flightcrew members; the proposed AD would limit ETOPS-180 to three flightcrew members and correct minimum oxygen dispatch pressure data. Comment period closed June 15, 2026; not yet a final rule.

references.effectivity: Airbus A330-201/-202/-203/-223/-243 and A330-301/-302/-303/-321/-322/-323/-341/-342/-343 airplanes MODIFIED under FAA STC ST04038NY (EFW P2F freighter conversion) only — not standard passenger configuration A330-300s
references.fetched_text_snippet: for airplanes with a flightcrew oxygen system supplied by a single oxygen cylinder, the oxygen supply would be insufficient under all circumstances for extended operations (ETOPS) with a maximum diversion time of 180 minutes (ETOPS-180) with four flightcrew members

records.root_cause: Single-cylinder flightcrew oxygen supply, combined with modified procedures from the EFW P2F freighter conversion (STC ST04038NY / EASA STC S10063798), found insufficient for ETOPS-180 diversion with four flightcrew members.

records.headline: UPS MD-11 (Flight 2976) crash investigation: NTSB hearing record remains under review; no new docket update this week
records.summary: NTSB investigation DCA26MA024 into the November 4, 2025 fatal crash of UPS Airlines Flight 2976 (MD-11) at Louisville remains open; a public investigative hearing was held May 19-20, 2026. NTSB's investigation page (last substantive update May 12, 2026, hearing agenda) shows no docket release, finding, or update dated within the current 2026-06-19 to 2026-06-26 window. FAA cleared the MD-11 type to resume flight in early May 2026 contingent on new spherical bearings and increased inspection frequency; no probable cause has been issued. Carried over per project convention as the major industry event of broad significance; explicitly flagged as not new this week.
records.oem_regulator_position: FAA cleared MD-11 to resume flight in early May 2026 contingent on installation of new spherical bearings and increased inspection frequency; NTSB has not yet issued a probable cause finding (confirmed via ntsb.gov investigation page, last updated through mid-May 2026, no in-window update found).
records.root_cause: Fatigue cracking reported (via trade press coverage of the May 19-20, 2026 hearing) to have originated in a lubrication channel inside an aft-mount spherical bearing within the MD-11 engine pylon; NTSB has not published a final root-cause finding.

records.headline: Cathay Pacific CX156 (A350-900, Brisbane-Hong Kong) severe turbulence event: HKCAD review pending, no in-window update
records.summary: Cathay Pacific flight CX156, an A350-900 (reg. B-LRV) flying Brisbane to Hong Kong, encountered severe turbulence approximately two hours from landing on May 23, 2026, injuring 10 (4 passengers, 6 unbuckled crew; 8 hospitalized). Cathay Pacific opened an internal investigation; trade press reports HKCAD is expected to review flight-recorder data as part of a formal inquiry. No HKCAD preliminary report, Cathay statement update, or other primary-source development was found dated within the current 2026-06-19 to 2026-06-26 window.
records.root_cause: Severe high-altitude turbulence encounter, reportedly difficult to detect via onboard weather radar; investigation into forecast accuracy, storm proximity, and crew response ongoing per trade press (no primary regulator document fetched).
